evals.kind: should-trigger, validates the 2026-07-29 body additions (Steps 1c/1d): the raw-looks-slower-than-the-whole-pipeline symptom is the giveaway that the PRINTER is being measured, not the computation; fix is to force each stage with a cheap consumer (SymProp.Statistics.size) and take per-stage cost as the delta between cumulative timings.

evals.query: I put four heavy Time Eval vm_compute commands in one probe file to compare a parameter sweep, and across two runs of the identical file the growth ratios came out completely different -- one run accelerating, the other decelerating. Which numbers do I trust?
evals.kind: should-trigger, validates the 2026-07-29 body addition (Step 1c): several heavy Evals in ONE coqc process contaminate each other via OCaml heap/GC state, so even the SHAPE of a curve becomes an artifact. Rule: one heavy reduction per coqc invocation. Distinct from Step 1b, which is about cross-FILE .vo page-cache noise; this entry guards that the intra-process case routes here too.

evals.query: To work out what's making symbolic execution slow, I want to patch the solver to skip the work I suspect and re-time it. How do I make sure the ablation is actually measuring what I think, rather than changing the shape of the proof term underneath me?
evals.kind: should-trigger, validates the 2026-07-29 body addition (Step 3b): a weakening ablation can cause path explosion (in CFGVer ~410 solver-killed forks per trip would come back to life) and a removal can truncate execution into an error leaf, both of which read as cost changes; fix is to prefer additive interventions and to census node kinds as a control, requiring every counter except the intended one to stay identical.

evals.query: I fixed both known scaling suspects in my CFGVer loop example -- the demonic-variable context is flat now and no register term duplicates across iterations -- but vm_compute cost still grows roughly quadratically with trip count. What else could be driving this, and is there already a fix?
evals.kind: should-trigger, validates the 2026-08-03 description CORRECTION: neither term duplication (Q80) nor |wctx| growth (Q98) is the dominant driver -- both were independently fixed/ruled out and the wall persisted. Root cause was a leaked `encodes_instr` heap chunk (is_duplicable := true, heap_extractions keeps duplicable chunks on consume, so the symbolic heap grows by one chunk per instruction step), now fixed by the landed chunk GC (PLAN-chunk-gc.md, chunk_gc/cchunk_gc run every step). This query describes a user who has already ruled out both prior suspects -- exactly the gap the old wctx-centric description left uncovered.
